origin: Original Teacher Workbench operational criteria; not a validated instrument

common.title: Target and evidence agree
common.pass_when: The task elicits the stated learning target and claimed standard; any alignment limit is explicit.

common.title: Content and keys are accurate
common.pass_when: Worked examples, accepted answers, units and scoring directions are correct and internally consistent.

common.title: Claims and sources are represented honestly
common.pass_when: External claims have supporting opened sources; authored tasks and uncertain observations are labeled.

common.title: Materials are usable
common.pass_when: The promised student tasks, source stimuli, teacher directions and timing are present and feasible.

common.title: Evidence supports the inference
common.pass_when: Individual learning, group products, behavior, simulation and missing evidence are distinguished; score claims stay within the data.

common.title: Participation and support are appropriate
common.pass_when: Required supports, privacy and developmentally appropriate directions are preserved; no unjustified exclusion or harmful labeling.

math.title: Mathematical meaning
math.pass_when: Representations, symbols and operations agree; explanation matches the mathematical construct.

math.title: Student reasoning
math.pass_when: Tasks require the reasoning warranted by the target and accept defensible strategies.

ela.title: Text evidence
ela.pass_when: Questions, models and keys are supported by the actual text or language evidence.

ela.title: Literacy construct
ela.pass_when: Decoding, fluency, comprehension and composition evidence are distinguished; scaffolds do not silently replace the target.

science.title: Scientific reasoning
science.pass_when: Phenomena, observations, data, units and explanations are accurate; conclusions follow from evidence.

science.title: Three-dimensional learning
science.pass_when: Where NGSS alignment is claimed, student work integrates the relevant practice, disciplinary idea and crosscutting concept.

humanities.title: Source reasoning
humanities.pass_when: Source identity, context and perspective are accurate; claims are distinguished from established evidence.

humanities.title: Evidence-based interpretation
humanities.pass_when: Tasks elicit sourcing, contextualization or corroboration as warranted, without treating all claims as equally supported.

access_language.title: Construct-preserving access
access_language.pass_when: Supports address a stated barrier and preserve required accommodations; changed constructs are disclosed.

access_language.title: Usable language support
access_language.pass_when: Language objectives and actual models/frames fit the content; fading applies to optional prompts, not required access.

formative.title: Diagnostic interpretation
formative.pass_when: Distractors and response patterns support tentative hypotheses; missing/ambiguous responses receive follow-up rather than unsupported labels.

formative.title: Actionable follow-up
formative.pass_when: The packet supplies a next teaching move and another task keyed to the observed evidence.

rehearsal.title: Simulation boundary
rehearsal.pass_when: Invented student responses and predicted outcomes are labeled as simulation or hypotheses.

rehearsal.title: Teacher practice
rehearsal.pass_when: Interactive mode gives space for the teacher to respond; feedback uses their actual move and supports a retry.

intervention.title: Need and intensity
intervention.pass_when: Activities match a documented target gap; tier, placement and cause are not inferred from a single score.

intervention.title: Implementation and monitoring
intervention.pass_when: The adult has models, keys, bounded scaffold decisions and feasible checks/regrouping rules.

grading.title: Policy and arithmetic
grading.pass_when: Calculation uses the declared policy, correctly handles missing/exempt evidence and can be reproduced.

grading.title: Defensible interpretation
grading.pass_when: Rollups retain coverage/support conditions; ordinal scales, growth and uncertainty are not misrepresented.
